title: Reduce size of Task Manager thumbnails when many are open and they start to become scrollable
line: When an app has many windows open, the Task Manager's window previews now get smaller so they fit on screen instead of scrolling right away.
explanation: Grouped window tooltips gave every thumbnail a fixed width of 16 grid units, so on a normal screen four or five windows already filled the width and the tooltip became a scrolling strip with most previews hidden. The change computes the thumbnail width from the screen width and the number of windows in the group, shrinking it (with the thumbnail height kept at half the width) down to a minimum of 10 grid units; only beyond that does the tooltip scroll. Single-window tooltips, vertical panels and text-only tooltips are unchanged.

commits.message:
applets/taskmanager: shrink grouped tooltip thumbnails before scrolling

Grouped window tooltips always used full size thumbnails, so a group of
just a few windows already made the tooltip scroll. Now the thumbnails
shrink to fit the screen, down to a minimum size, before it scrolls.

BUG: 524372

patches.diff:
From c8c2b46679b56980b08fc9960e292ad828db525e Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 19:22:37 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] applets/taskmanager: shrink grouped tooltip thumbnails before
 scrolling

Grouped window tooltips always used full size thumbnails, so a group of
just a few windows already made the tooltip scroll. Now the thumbnails
shrink to fit the screen, down to a minimum size, before it scrolls.

BUG: 524372
---
 applets/taskmanager/qml/ToolTipDelegate.qml | 14 ++++++++++++--
 applets/taskmanager/qml/ToolTipInstance.qml |  2 +-
 2 files changed, 13 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)

diff --git a/applets/taskmanager/qml/ToolTipDelegate.qml b/applets/taskmanager/qml/ToolTipDelegate.qml
index 014e954c5c..ea00cbcee5 100644
--- a/applets/taskmanager/qml/ToolTipDelegate.qml
+++ b/applets/taskmanager/qml/ToolTipDelegate.qml
@@ -53,8 +53,18 @@ Loader {
     property bool blockingUpdates: false
 
     readonly property bool isVerticalPanel: Plasmoid.formFactor === PlasmaCore.Types.Vertical
-    // This number controls the overall size of the window tooltips
-    readonly property int tooltipInstanceMaximumWidth: Kirigami.Units.gridUnit * 16
+    // This number controls the overall size of the window tooltips. Thumbnails of
+    // a group shrink down to a minimum width before the tooltip starts to scroll.
+    readonly property int tooltipInstanceMaximumWidth: {
+        const defaultWidth = Kirigami.Units.gridUnit * 16
+        if (!isGroup || isVerticalPanel || !Plasmoid.configuration.showToolTips || windows.length < 2) {
+            return defaultWidth
+        }
+        // 2 * Kirigami.Units.smallSpacing is for the margin of tooltipDialog
+        const availableWidth = Screen.desktopAvailableWidth - 2 * Kirigami.Units.smallSpacing
+        const fittingWidth = Math.floor((availableWidth + Kirigami.Units.gridUnit) / windows.length) - Kirigami.Units.gridUnit
+        return Math.max(Kirigami.Units.gridUnit * 10, Math.min(defaultWidth, fittingWidth))
+    }
 
     // These properties are required to make tooltip interactive when there is a player but no window is present.
     readonly property Mpris.PlayerContainer playerData: mpris2Source.playerForLauncherUrl(launcherUrl, pidParent)
diff --git a/applets/taskmanager/qml/ToolTipInstance.qml b/applets/taskmanager/qml/ToolTipInstance.qml
index 5a42d24a17..78e09477d5 100644
--- a/applets/taskmanager/qml/ToolTipInstance.qml
+++ b/applets/taskmanager/qml/ToolTipInstance.qml
@@ -287,7 +287,7 @@ ColumnLayout {
         id: thumbnailSourceItem
 
         Layout.fillWidth: true
-        Layout.preferredHeight: Kirigami.Units.gridUnit * 8
+        Layout.preferredHeight: toolTipDelegate.tooltipInstanceMaximumWidth / 2
 
         clip: true
         visible: Plasmoid.configuration.showToolTips && toolTipDelegate.isWin
-- 
2.53.0

media.caption: Six Konsole windows: the tooltip is cut off and scrolls
Six Konsole windows: smaller previews, all visible, no scrollbar
Nine windows: previews at their minimum size, then the tooltip scrolls
Two windows: previews keep their normal size

review.text: Clean, concise QML fix that dynamically shrinks horizontal grouped window tooltip thumbnails down to `10 * gridUnit` before scrolling, using a formula that matches `ScrollView.maximumWidth` and `estimatedWidth` exactly while keeping the 2:1 thumbnail aspect ratio in `ToolTipInstance.qml`. There are no binding loops, single-window/vertical/text-only tooltips remain untouched, and the 2-, 6-, and 9-window screenshots confirm the behavior.

reviews.text: Clean, concise QML fix that dynamically shrinks horizontal grouped window tooltip thumbnails down to `10 * gridUnit` before scrolling, using a formula that matches `ScrollView.maximumWidth` and `estimatedWidth` exactly while keeping the 2:1 thumbnail aspect ratio in `ToolTipInstance.qml`. There are no binding loops, single-window/vertical/text-only tooltips remain untouched, and the 2-, 6-, and 9-window screenshots confirm the behavior.

The approach (shrink grouped thumbnails to a 10-gridUnit floor before falling back to scrolling, height kept at width/2) matches the wish and the screenshots show it working on a single 1280x800 screen. But the fitting width is computed from Screen.desktopAvailableWidth, which is the available width of the whole virtual desktop (all outputs on Wayland), not the screen the panel is on. On a common two-monitor setup the thumbnails would not shrink until about twice as many windows, and the tooltip would still overflow its screen, so the fix doesn't hold for multi-monitor users. Single-window, vertical-panel and text-only paths stay as they were, and the commit message matches the diff.
changes: Compute availableWidth from the tooltip/panel's own screen (e.g. Screen.width or the screen's availableGeometry), not Screen.desktopAvailableWidth, and ideally switch scrollView.maximumWidth to the same metric so the shrink and scroll thresholds agree
Verify on a two-output rig (e.g. a second kvout virtual output) that previews shrink to fit the panel's screen
